source.description: Publish() marshals a Sample struct to YAML via yaml.Marshal and sends the bytes to the aurora.telemetry.tenant bus topic via bus.Send(). The Go producer itself is safe (yaml.Marshal of a typed struct cannot produce !!python/object payloads); however, the bus topic is an open network channel — any bus client that can publish to the topic (including compromised or external producers not present in this delivery) can send arbitrary bytes. The consumer trusts all messages equally.

hops.note: bus.Send(TenantTopic, body) transmits the YAML payload across the aurora.telemetry.tenant bus topic. This is a confirmed cross-component seam (crossComponent: true in link graph, resolved by secondary literal-match pass). The receiving component is aurora-portal.
consume() subscribes to TENANT_TOPIC via bus.subscribe() and yields each received message to handle(). No schema validation, type check, or size limit is applied to message.body before forwarding.
handle() receives the message object; message.body carries the raw bus payload. No sanitisation is applied between receipt and deserialisation.

sink.description: yaml.load(message.body) called without a Loader argument. PyYAML's default Loader supports !!python/object/apply and related tags; a malicious publisher on the aurora.telemetry.tenant bus topic can achieve arbitrary Python code execution in the aurora-portal consumer process.
